name: Eastern Katu
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Wallace, Judith M. 1969. Katu phonemes. Mon-Khmer Studies 3; Nguyen Huu Hoanh & Nguyen Van Loi 1998 Tieng Katu (grammar). sealang.net archive down (SIL 403)

new_statements.quote: The Katu word has a main syllable which can be preceded by one, two or three presyllables. The word can be symbolised as CV3/CV2/CV1/MS. CV3 and CV2 are always affixes, whereas CV1 is rarely an affix. Presyllables are always unstressed. The main syllable MS can be symbolised as CV±C or CCV.
new_statements.citation: Costello, Nancy A. 1991. Nooq Paraaq Katu / Katu Dictionary: Katu-Vietnamese-English (Tủ Sách Ngôn-Ngữ Dân-Tộc Thiểu-Số Việt-Nam, cuốn 5, phần 2). Manila: Summer Institute of Linguistics.
new_statements.locator: Front matter, section 'Orthography', subsection 'Word Structure and Phoneme Distribution' (unnumbered page; p. 1 of the 3-page Rosetta Project excerpt rosettaproject_ktv_ortho-1)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Katu words are sesquisyllabic: a full main syllable (CV(C) or CCV) optionally preceded by up to three reduced presyllables (mostly affixes). Presyllables are never stressed, so stress falls on the main syllable, which is always the last syllable of the word (i.e. word-final stress in every polysyllable; monosyllables are the main syllable).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the statement is absolute ('always unstressed').
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (dictionary headwords/citation forms); the dictionary covers Low Katu of An-Diem (default, unmarked) and Phu-Hoa, plus High Katu (hk), all in Quang Nam, Vietnam. The statement is a one-line word-structure note in a dictionary's orthography preface, not a full phonological analysis; the dedicated phonology paper (Wallace 1969, 'Katu phonemes') could not be opened.
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding source (Costello 1991 dictionary) describes the Vietnam Katu of Quang Nam province: Low Katu of An-Diem (default) and Phu-Hoa, plus High Katu; all fall under Glottolog east1236 (Eastern Katu, ktv; alternate names include High Katu, Kantu, Phuong). Costello & Sulavan 1996 states the Lao PDR dialect differs only in a few predictable phonetic details (presyllable inventory reduced to one presyllable). Western Katu (west2398, kuf) is a separate Glottolog language and is not what these sources describe.

sources.note: Phoneme inventory and word structure (main syllable optionally preceded by one presyllable in Lao Katu, up to three in Vietnam Katu; presyllable vowel /a/ is short and unglottalized) but no explicit statement about stress; no text layer, scanned at 300 dpi.
